lines: The Moon Lantern shone on the balcony. A blue moon picture lit up, then a gold sun picture. The two lights jumped onto the garden path. Then the path went dark.
The Sunrise Arch lights the way to the garden gate each morning. Let’s catch the moon and sun lights so we can see how the path should work.
We caught blue moon, gold sun, blue moon, gold sun. They took turns. Now we can follow the dark path and find out why it stopped.
Mia, Sol and Tavi followed the dark stones to a turning gate. Vee hurried over with one round path tile.
Hello! I’m Vee. I look after this path. One side of my tile has a blue moon. The other side has a gold sun. Help me take a picture of each side.
Both pictures are in my notebook. It is one tile with two different sides. Their names help us tell them apart.
The first gate was stuck. Vee put the tile inside with the blue moon facing up.
The curved handle turns the tile over. Pull the handle all the way to the gold mark, then release it.
The gate turned the tile over once. The blue moon went underneath, and the gold sun came out on top.
Three short paths led forward. One missed the next gate. One went through it once. One looped through it twice.
We need one more turn. Choose a path, then send the gold sun tile through it. Watch which side comes back.
The gold sun turned over once, and the blue moon came back. Return means the side we saw earlier is showing again.
The working stones showed blue moon, gold sun, blue moon, gold sun. Three dark stones waited next.
Look from left to right. Put the next three lights on the path. Use the same turn-over rule the gate showed us.
Blue moon, gold sun, blue moon came next. The path follows a pattern. Pattern means a rule that tells us what comes next.
Sol hurried ahead and placed six tiles. Two matching pictures met in one place, so the light stopped. His whole first try stayed where everyone could see it.
Start at the left and check each move. Find the first tile that stops taking turns, then replace only that tile.
We kept Sol's first try, found the first broken move, and repaired only that tile. Now the light can move again.
The light reached a bridge. The first sign showed whether Vee should start over or under. After each arch, the safe path had to change.
Move me onto the path shown by the first sign. Then change between over and under as I cross. A closed gate will stop me safely.
Vee changed between over and under all the way across. The pictures changed, but the two roles still took turns.
At the last gate, three route maps lay side by side. One stopped before the arch. One put matching lights together. One reached the arch and kept taking turns.
Check where each route ends. Then check its lights from left to right. Choose one map and send Vee to test it.
Route C follows every turn and reaches the Sunrise Arch. The repaired light trail is complete.
The light reached the Sunrise Arch. Four empty windows opened. A star and a leaf waited beside them.
First build a star-and-leaf row that takes turns. Then remember the first gate: a blue moon went in and the tile turned over once. Which side came out?
Star and leaf took turns, and gold sun came out after blue moon turned over once. The pictures changed, but the rule did not. The Sunrise Arch is shining!

Here is the lesson. A pattern is a rule that tells us what comes next. We watched moon and sun take turns, turned one tile to see its other side, saw the first side return, repaired the first move that broke the rule, and used the same rule with over and under, then star and leaf. This matters because a clear rule helps us predict what comes next and find where a mistake began.
